page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.8xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processors running at an unboosted baseline clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance configuration supplies 32 virtual CPUs derived from 16 physical cores via multithreading, along with 256 GB of main system memory. This architecture yields a high 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 8 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is strictly network-attached, as the instance includes no local storage volumes. Dedicated baseline network throughput is rated at 6 Gbps, and the configuration contains zero GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks show a pronounced divergence between single-thread throughput and concurrent multicore operations. Reflecting its 2.5 GHz clock speed, single-core metrics fall into lower percentiles, as demonstrated by a stress-ng single-core score of 1,106.99 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1,018.0. Similarly, single-threaded gzip compression performs poorly at 19.13 GB/sec. However, parallel workloads scale cleanly across all 32 vCPUs. The instance records 23,622.2 in stress-ng multicore, 8,927.0 in Geekbench multicore, and a PassMark CPU score of 23,157.62. Memory throughput is solid, delivering 1,312.67 GB/sec on cached 16 KB read blocks and 99.19 GB/sec on large 256 MB read blocks. In-memory databases register responsive scaling, with Redis achieving 22.7 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency and architectural standpoint, the instance trades high single-thread clock rates for high memory density and stable multithreaded capacity. It delivers favorable economics for workloads bounded by RAM footprint rather than peak per-core instructions. The absence of integrated local NVMe storage requires external disk allocation for persistent persistence layers. Hardware vector instruction sets including AVX-512 and VNNI allow modest integer and inference tasks, reaching 80.05 tokens per second for text generation on lightweight 135M models. Consequently, ecs.se1ne.8xlarge is suited for in-memory databases, large-scale caching services like Redis, memory-intensive batch processing, enterprise ERP backends, and multi-threaded analytical queries.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.8xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the x86_64 architecture using dedicated Intel Xeon 8269CY processors clocked at 2.5 GHz. It delivers 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading and provides 256 GB of system RAM, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. The instance includes 6 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, operates without GPUs, and features no local storage. Benchmark results illustrate average multi-core CPU and memory throughput alongside lower single-core execution speeds, marked by a Geekbench multi-core result of 8,927.0 and Redis performance reaching 22.7 million operations per second. While single-threaded tasks face latency tradeoffs from moderate clock speeds, the aggregate compute capacity and expansive RAM pool offer cost-effective density for memory-bound deployments. This profile fits memory-centric services, including in-memory data grids, Redis caches, distributed enterprise applications, and mid-sized transactional databases requiring expansive memory footprints without requiring local NVMe disks.
